description: Extraction pollution insecure rights and weak enforcement accelerate resource degradation.
Climate extremes and market disruption produce acute food insecurity.
Drought aquifer depletion and competing demand intensify conflict.
Speculation carbon markets and large land acquisition increase dispossession.
Output rises while soil water biodiversity and livelihoods deteriorate.
Technology improves monitoring and productivity but introduces dependency and exclusion risk.
Food water land restoration and rights-based governance reinforce resilience.
Watershed restoration local food infrastructure and community governance reduce stress.
